categories.name: Reader promise and original contribution
categories.evidence: The control-ownership test and reusable boundary card give readers a decision artifact beyond a definition survey.

categories.name: Technical correctness and nuance
categories.evidence: The corrected state machine consumes budgets, fails closed on denial, matches approvals, preserves operation identity, and refuses unverified completion; production persistence and identity verification remain explicit limitations.

categories.name: Knowledge depth and progression
categories.evidence: The lesson progresses from interface ambiguity to operational definition, loop, state machine, worked trace, failure boundaries, and architecture choice without requiring a framework.

categories.name: Reproducibility and runnable evidence
categories.evidence: A standard-library implementation and seven deterministic tests cover success, approval, denial, failure exhaustion, unknown outcome retry, budget termination, and false completion.

categories.name: Failures, trade-offs, and evaluation
categories.evidence: The trace and failure table separate planning, policy, tool, state, distributed-write, and verification failures while explaining when a deterministic workflow is preferable.

categories.name: Pedagogy and transfer
categories.evidence: Observable outcomes align with the worked case, boundary-card exercise, self-check, retrieval questions, and transfer prompt.

categories.name: Visual explanation and accessibility
categories.evidence: Two captioned SVG diagrams provide a system comparison and state-transition view with equivalent descriptions and editable Draw.io sources.

categories.name: Evidence and publishing trust
categories.evidence: Primary guidance, bounded practitioner synthesis, a claim register, tested versions, AI disclosure, and explicit implementation limitations support reader trust.
